stemMd: What is the smallest positive integer n for which 18n is a perfect square?
explanationMd: Factor 18 = 2 × 3². A perfect square requires even prime exponents, so only one additional factor of two is needed. Then 18 × 2 = 36. Any smaller positive integer is one, which does not work.

distractorRationale.b: Eighteen times three is fifty-four, not a square.
distractorRationale.c: This leaves odd prime exponents in the factorization.
distractorRationale.d: Eighteen times nine still has an odd exponent of two.
distractorRationale.e: This works but is not the smallest positive multiplier.
